name: qanvas
description: A friendly visual quantum circuit builder in your browser: drag gates, see results live, step through with explanations, and copy Qiskit, Cirq, pyQuil or OpenQASM code. Works offline, in English and Spanish.

paragraphs: A friendly visual quantum circuit builder that runs in your browser. Drag gates onto qubits, watch the results update live, step through the circuit with plain-language explanations, and copy working Qiskit, Cirq, pyQuil or OpenQASM code.

The visual tools students meet first tend to look and feel dated, and the polished ones need an account and a connection. Qanvas is built for students first and researchers second: no account, no install, works offline, in English and Spanish. It's the circuit builder of quantum-lab, and it also runs on its own.

Everything works with the keyboard too: focus a gate, press Space to pick it up, move with the arrow keys and press Space to drop it. Ctrl/⌘ + Z undoes, Ctrl/⌘ + C and V copy and paste, and Delete removes the selected gate.
features: Build circuits with up to 12 qubits (24 in quantum-lab): H, X, Y, Z, S, S†, T, T†, Rx, Ry, Rz and P with any angle, CNOT, CZ, SWAP, Toffoli and measurement. Drag from the palette, move, copy, delete, undo and redo.
Step through the circuit with the slider. In Learn mode, a short explanation at each step says what the gate did, with the state before and after.

Copy or download code in Qiskit, Cirq, pyQuil or OpenQASM 2.0, with the line for the current step highlighted. Downloads include a ready-to-run notebook or Python script that runs the circuit and counts the outcomes.
Edit the OpenQASM code directly: the circuit updates when you pause typing, and keeps its last valid version while the code has a mistake.
Start from an example: Bell state, GHZ, superdense coding, quantum teleportation, Deutsch–Jozsa and Grover search, each with a "Try this" challenge.
